gloss: turn (the face); face, front; before, in the presence of
summary: פָּנָה is to turn: to turn and go, turn to look, turn toward someone in favour or toward other gods, and of the day, to turn toward evening; its participle is “facing” a direction, and the piel turns things out of the way, so “clear, prepare a way” (Isa 40:3; Mal 3:1). פָּנִים, always plural, is the face, the side a person or thing turns toward others: a man’s face and countenance, the person himself present, the surface of the earth, the front of a building; and with prepositions לִפְנֵי “before, in the presence of” and מִפְּנֵי “from before, because of”, the words by which the feasts of Lev 23 are kept “before Yahweh” and the ark goes before Israel (Num 10:33–35). Yahweh’s face shining on his people is his favour, his hiding it is his turning away, and “turn to me and be saved” is his call to all the ends of the earth (Num 6:25–26; Isa 45:22). Akkadian pānu, Ugaritic pn and Phoenician pnm “face, front”, with lpn “before” in each, answer to the noun and its prepositions.

words.gloss: face; countenance; presence, person; surface, front; (לְפָנִים) formerly
words.summary: Always plural in form. The face as the turned side of a person, and so the person as present to others; of things, their surface or front. With prepositions it makes the commonest words for “before” (see לִפְנֵי, מִפְּנֵי).

senses.definition: The front of the head of a man or living creature: what falls in anger, is covered, veiled, spat in, or shines.

evidence.note: Cain burned with anger “and his פָּנִים fell”; Yahweh asks why his face is fallen (Gen 4:6).
Judah took Tamar for a harlot “because she had covered her פָּנִים”.
Moses did not know that the skin of his פָּנִים shone; he put a veil over it (Exo 34:33–35).
Paul expounds Exo 34: Israel could not look intently at the πρόσωπον of Moses for its glory.
Elijah wrapped his face in his mantle.
“If her father had but spit in her face”.
Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him.
The living creatures’ four faces, of a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle; echoed in Rev 4:7.

senses.definition: The face as it shows the heart: glad or sad, and turned toward or away from someone.

evidence.note: “A merry heart makes a good פָּנִים, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.”
“Why is your face sad, seeing you are not sick? This is nothing but sorrow of heart.”
Hannah ate, “and her face was no more” sad.
“I will leave off my face and be cheerful.”
Jacob saw Laban’s face, that it was not toward him as before; Jacob repeats it to his wives (Gen 31:5).

senses.definition: The face standing for the one whose face it is, present in person: to go with someone, or to meet and speak “face to face”.

evidence.note: “My פָּנִים will go, and I will give you rest”; Moses: “If your face does not go, do not bring us up from here” (Exo 33:15).
Hushai to Absalom: “and your פָּנִים going into battle”, that is, you in person.
He brought you out of Egypt “by his face, by his great power”.
Yahweh spoke to Moses פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִים, “as a man speaks to his friend”.
Yahweh spoke with all Israel “face to face” at the mountain, out of the fire.
Jacob names the place Peniel: “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
Gideon has seen the angel of Yahweh face to face.
Yahweh will plead with Israel “face to face” in the wilderness of the peoples.
“Now through a mirror darkly, but then πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον”: the Hebrew phrase in Greek.

senses.definition: Yahweh’s face turned toward people: shining or lifted up on them, it is his favour and their saving; hidden, it is his turning away; set against them, his hostility. To seek his face is to seek him, and to appear before it is to come to his house.

evidence.note: “Yahweh make his face shine on you and be gracious to you; Yahweh lift up his face on you and give you peace” (Num 6:25–26).

senses.definition: His face made to shine or lifted on someone, set beside his grace, his saving and his blessing.

evidence.note: “Restore us, O God, and cause your face to shine, and we shall be saved”; the refrain again in Psa 80:8, 20.
“God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause his face to shine on us.”
“Lift up the light of your face on us.”
Not their sword but “your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, for you favoured them”.
“That times of refreshing may come from the πρόσωπον of the Lord.”
God has shone in our hearts “to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the πρόσωπον of Jesus Christ”.

senses.definition: Yahweh hides his face from a people or a man for their sin, leaving them to their enemies; its end is his face no more hidden.

evidence.note: “I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured”; “because they have turned (פָּנָה) to other gods” (Deu 31:18).
“Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you.”
“How long will you hide your face from me?”
“In a flood of wrath I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have mercy on you.”
“I will not hide my face from them any more, for I have poured out my spirit on the house of Israel.”

senses.definition: Yahweh sets his face against a man or a city to cut it off.

evidence.note: “I will set my face against that soul that eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people.”
Against the soul that turns (פָּנָה) to mediums.
“The face of Yahweh is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth”; quoted in 1Pe 3:12.

senses.definition: To seek his face is to seek him in prayer and turning from evil; to appear before his face is to come to him at his feasts; to see his face is promised the righteous.

evidence.note: “Seek my face.” “Your face, Yahweh, I will seek.”
If my people humble themselves, pray, seek my face and turn from their evil ways.
Three times a year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord Yahweh; not empty (Exo 23:15; Deu 16:16).
“When shall I come and appear before the face of God?”
“You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live”; “my face shall not be seen” (Exo 33:23).
“I will behold your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied when I awake with your likeness.”
“The upright shall behold his face.”
“They shall see his πρόσωπον, and his name shall be on their foreheads.”

senses.definition: The upturned side of the earth, the ground or the deep, which things lie on or cover.

evidence.note: Darkness on the face of the deep, the spirit of God moving on the face of the waters.
A mist watered the whole face of the ground.
Every living thing on the face of the ground was blotted out in the flood.
The dove found no rest, “for the waters were on the face of the whole earth”.

senses.definition: The front of a thing, the side toward the one approaching: of a turban, a building, a battle line; once the edge of an iron tool.

evidence.note: The gold plate is on the front of the turban (אֶל־מוּל פְּנֵי־הַמִּצְנֶפֶת).
The porch before the nave of the house.
Joab saw that “the face of the battle” was against him before and behind.
If the iron is blunt and he does not whet the פָּנִים: its edge.
They went backward (לְאָחוֹר) and not forward (לְפָנִים).

senses.definition: With לְ, what lies in front in time, which Hebrew sees as what has gone before: formerly, in former times.

evidence.note: “לְפָנִים in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God… for he who is now called a prophet was לְפָנִים called a seer.”
The Emim dwelt there in times past.
Hazor was formerly the head of all those kingdoms.
The name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath Arba; so Jdg 1:10.
“This was the custom לְפָנִים in Israel concerning redeeming and exchanging.”
“Of old (לְפָנִים) you laid the foundation of the earth”; Heb 1:10 quotes it, κατ’ ἀρχάς, of the Son.

evidence.locator: פָּנֶה (פָּנִים) → πρόσωπον ×923 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Num.6.25, Gen.32.31

evidence.note: At the transfiguration “his πρόσωπον shone as the sun”, as Moses’ face shone (Exo 34:29).
“We all, with unveiled πρόσωπον beholding the glory of the Lord”, after Moses’ veil (Exo 34:33–35).
“He set his πρόσωπον to go to Jerusalem”: the Hebrew שָׂם פָּנִים (Jer 42:15; 2Ki 12:18); Luk 9:53, “his face was going to Jerusalem”.
Christ entered heaven itself, now to appear in the πρόσωπον of God for us.
Their angels always behold the πρόσωπον of my Father.
“You do not receive πρόσωπον”: the Hebrew נָשָׂא פָנִים, “lift the face”.
“God does not receive the πρόσωπον of man.”

parallels.note: Yahweh’s eyes toward the righteous, his face against evildoers.
His face shining set beside his being gracious.

opposites.note: The back against the face: Moses sees Yahweh’s back, not his face; Israel went backward, not forward.
“They have turned to me the back of the neck and not the face.”

phrases.gloss: face to face: in person, without go-between
lift up the face: accept a person, grant his request; in judgment, show partiality

evidence.note: “I have lifted up your face in this thing also”: granted Lot’s request.
Jacob: “perhaps he will lift up my face”, accept me.
“You shall not lift up the face of the poor, nor honour the face of the mighty.”
God “does not lift up faces nor take a bribe”.
A nation fierce of face that will not lift up the face of the old.
The idiom in Greek: God is no προσωπολήμπτης, “receiver of faces”; so Rom 2:11, Jas 2:1.

phrases.gloss: recognise faces: show partiality in judgment
cause the face to shine: show favour
hide the face: withdraw favour, refuse to hear
seek the face: seek someone’s presence and favour
set the face: be resolved to go somewhere; (with בְּ) set oneself against

evidence.note: Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

phrases.gloss: entreat the face (of Yahweh): plead for his favour
fall on the face: bow to the ground in reverence or entreaty

evidence.note: The disciples ἔπεσον ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν.

phrases.gloss: the bread of the face: the bread set before Yahweh continually

evidence.note: “Bread of the face before my face always.”

phrases.gloss: on the face of; in front of, east of; in the presence of, beside

evidence.note: Machpelah “before Mamre”.
“In the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising.”
Haran died “in the presence of” Terah his father.
“You shall have no other gods before my face.”

words.gloss: before, in front of; in the presence of; before (in time)
words.summary: לְ + פְּנֵי, “to the face of”: in front of someone, or in his presence, and so earlier than. Its uses are counted under פָּנִים, under whose key the text files them. It is the word of the feasts of Lev 23, kept “before Yahweh”, and of the ark going before Israel (Num 10:33). Ugaritic and Phoenician lpn and Akkadian ana pān(i) are built the same way.

senses.definition: In front of, ahead of someone, of going before to lead or clear the way.

evidence.note: “The ark of the covenant of Yahweh went before them three days’ journey, to search out a resting place for them.”
The angel of God who went before the camp moved and went behind them.
“I send an angel before you, to keep you in the way.”
The priests bearing the ark before the people.
Yahweh goes over before you as a consuming fire.
“He will prepare the way before me”; quoted Mat 11:10, ἔμπροσθέν σου.
John: “I am sent before him (ἔμπροσθεν ἐκείνου).”

senses.gloss: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)
senses.definition: In the sight and presence of someone: standing to serve a king or Yahweh, and doing an act of worship where he is.

evidence.note: “As Yahweh the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand”; again 1Ki 18:15.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh.
Levi separated “to stand before Yahweh to minister to him”.
The priest waves the sheaf “before Yahweh, for your acceptance”; the bread of the firstfruits likewise (Lev 23:20).
The Day of the coverings, “to make a covering for you before Yahweh your God”.
At the feast of booths, “you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God seven days”.
At the alarm of the trumpets “you shall be remembered before Yahweh your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies”.
The trumpets over the offerings are “a memorial before your God”.
“I am Gabriel, who stands ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ”, Elijah’s phrase (1Ki 17:1).

senses.definition: Earlier than an event or another person.

evidence.note: “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall”; so Pro 18:12.
Two years before the earthquake.
To give the younger before the firstborn.
“I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of Yahweh.”

senses.definition: With “give”: deliver an enemy before someone, into his power.

evidence.note: “When Yahweh your God delivers them before you, you shall strike them.”

evidence.locator: פָּנֶה (פָּנִים, chiefly as לִפְנֵי) → ἐνώπιον ×212 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Exo.33.11, 1Ki.8.28

evidence.note: John “shall be great ἐνώπιον the Lord”.
He shall go before him (ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ) in the spirit and power of Elijah (Mal 3:23).
Mal 3:1 quoted: “who shall prepare your way before you”.

words.gloss: from before, away from; because of
words.summary: מִן + פְּנֵי, “from the face of”: fleeing or being driven from before someone, and so the cause something comes from. Its uses are counted under פָּנִים. Akkadian pānu carries the same “from before” and “because of”.

senses.definition: Away from someone’s face or presence: fleeing from him, driven out from before him.

evidence.note: When the ark set out: “Rise up, Yahweh, let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee from before you”; Psa 68:2 takes up the words.
Yahweh casts out many nations from before you.
Cain went out from the presence of Yahweh.
“Let us flee from the face of Israel.”

senses.definition: The cause from which something comes or flees.

evidence.note: “The earth is filled with violence because of them (מִפְּנֵיהֶם).”
Noah went into the ark “because of the waters of the flood”.
Their cry “because of their taskmasters”.

words.gloss: turn; turn to, regard; face; (piel) clear, prepare

stems.gloss: turn; turn to, regard; face (a direction); decline (of the day)

senses.definition: Turn the body to go another way, often “turn and go, turn and journey”.

evidence.note: “Turn and take your journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorites.”
“You have compassed this mountain long enough; turn northward.”
Pharaoh turned and went into his house.
The men turned from there and went toward Sodom.
After the Passover, “in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents”.
Moses turned and went down from the mountain with the tablets.
Naaman turned and went away in a rage.
“That I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”
“Where has your beloved turned?”

senses.definition: Turn the face toward something to see it.

evidence.note: Moses “turned this way and that way, and saw that there was no man”.
They turned toward the wilderness, “and behold, the glory of Yahweh appeared in the cloud”; so Num 17:7.
Aaron turned toward Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
Abner looked behind him.
Judah looked back, and the battle was before and behind.
“Look upon me, for I will not lie to your face.”
“I turned to all my works that my hands had done… and behold, all was vanity”; so Ecc 2:12.

senses.definition: Turn one’s face toward a person, his prayer or his offering: give heed to it, favour it. Said above all of Yahweh, and set beside his being gracious and hearing.

evidence.note: “I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you and establish my covenant with you.”
“Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am alone and afflicted”; so Psa 86:16; 119:132.
“Turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, to hear the cry.”
“He has turned to the prayer of the destitute, and not despised their prayer.”
Yahweh was gracious to them and turned to them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Yahweh turned to Gideon: “Go in this your might.”
To the mountains of Israel: “I am for you, and I will turn to you.”
Moses: “Do not turn to their offering.”
“He no longer turns to the offering, or receives it with good will from your hand.”
“Do not look to the stubbornness of this people.”
“You looked for much, and behold, little.”

senses.definition: Turn to something other than Yahweh for worship or counsel: idols, other gods, mediums.

evidence.note: “Do not turn to idols, nor make yourselves molten gods.”
“Do not turn to mediums or spiritists.”
The soul that turns to mediums, “I will set my face against that soul”.
Yahweh hides his face “because they have turned to other gods”; so Deu 31:20.
A heart that turns away today from Yahweh to serve the gods of the nations.
Yahweh loves Israel, “though they turn to other gods”.
Blessed the man who “does not turn to the proud”.
“Take heed, do not turn to iniquity.”
“To which of the holy ones will you turn?”

senses.gloss: turn to Yahweh; turn each to his own way
senses.definition: The whole man turned toward Yahweh to be saved by him, or turned away, each to his own way; to turn the back and not the face is to refuse him.

evidence.note: “Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.”
“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned each one to his own way, and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.”
Peter expounds Isa 53:6: “you were as sheep going astray, but have now returned to the shepherd of your souls” (Peshitta אֶתְפְּנִיתוּן, the Syriac of this root).
The shepherds “all turn to their own way, each to his gain”.
“They have turned to me the back and not the face”; so Jer 32:33.

senses.definition: Turn round in retreat or flight.

evidence.note: They turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon; so Jdg 20:47.
“Each man will turn to his own people, and each flee to his own land”; so Jer 50:16.

senses.definition: Of things set in a direction: oxen, gates, chambers, a boundary turned toward a quarter.

evidence.note: The sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three west, three south, three east; so 2Ch 4:4.
“The gate that faces toward the east.”
The gate of the inner court that faces east, shut the six working days.
The wheels went where the head faced; they did not turn as they went.
The border turned toward Gilgal.
One company of raiders turned toward Ophrah; so 1Sa 13:18.
A vine whose branches turned toward him.

senses.definition: Of morning or evening coming on, and of days passing: “the turning of the morning, of the evening”.

evidence.note: Isaac went out to meditate in the field “at the turning of the evening (לִפְנוֹת עָרֶב)”.
“At the turning of the evening he shall bathe in water, and when the sun is down he may come into the camp.”
“God will help her at the turning of the morning.”
The sea returned to its strength at the turning of the morning.
“Woe to us, for the day turns away, the shadows of the evening are stretched out.”
“All our days have turned away in your wrath.”

senses.definition: Turn things out of a place to make it free: empty a house, make room, clear ground before a vine; once, clear away an enemy.

evidence.note: Laban: “I have cleared the house, and room for the camels.”
They shall empty the house before the priest comes in to see the plague, that all in it be not made unclean.
Of the vine brought out of Egypt: “You cleared before it, and it took deep root and filled the land.”
“Yahweh has taken away your judgments, he has cleared away your enemy.”

senses.definition: Clear the way of obstacles before one who is coming, of Yahweh’s coming and of his people’s return; the New Testament reads it “prepare” of John going before Jesus.

evidence.note: “A voice cries: In the wilderness clear the way of Yahweh, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
“Build up, build up, clear the way, take up the stumbling block out of the way of my people”; so Isa 62:10, “gather out the stones”.
“Behold, I send my messenger, and he will clear the way before me; and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.”
Isa 40:3 of John the Baptist: ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου; so Mrk 1:3, Luk 3:4, Jhn 1:23.
Mal 3:1 of John: ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου, “who shall prepare your way”; the Septuagint has ἐπιβλέψεται “look upon”, and the gospels read the Hebrew piel instead. So Mrk 1:2; Luk 7:27.
“You will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.”

senses.definition: Make something turn: tails set to tails, a shoulder turned to go, a neck turned in flight.

evidence.note: Samson “turned tail to tail” and put a torch between each pair.
When Saul turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart.
“How Moab has turned the back with shame!”

senses.definition: Of an army or city turning round in rout; with a negative, not to turn round at all.

evidence.note: “They fled apace and did not look back.”
Damascus “has turned to flee”.
Fathers do not turn back to their children for feebleness of hands.
“Stand, stand!” but none turns back.

senses.definition: Be set facing a direction; or, as a cry to fugitives, be turned back.

evidence.note: The upper gate “which faces north” (מָפְנֶה).
“Flee, turn back, dwell deep, inhabitants of Dedan.”

evidence.locator: פָּנָה → ἐπιβλέπω ×16 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Lev.26.9, 1Ki.8.28, Psa.25.16 (ἐπίβλεψον)

evidence.note: “He has regarded (ἐπέβλεψεν) the low estate of his handmaid.”

evidence.locator: פָּנָה → ἐπιστρέφω ×14 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Isa.45.22 ἐπιστράφητε

evidence.note: “Repent and turn (ἐπιστρέψατε), that your sins may be blotted out.”
“How you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God”: the opposite of Lev 19:4.

evidence.locator: פָּנָה (piel) → ἑτοιμάζω; Gen.24.31 ἡτοίμακα, Isa.40.3 ἑτοιμάσατε

parallels.note: “Turn to me and be gracious to me.”
Turning to a prayer is hearing it.

phrases.gloss: at the turning of evening / of morning
turn the back of the neck: turn away, refuse

words.summary: The inner one of two: the inner house, court, gate or rooms of the temple and the palace. How it comes from “face, front” is not shown: no verse links them and no cognate shares the sense “inner”, so its tie to the root rests on its form alone. The Septuagint’s ἐσώτερος carries it into Hebrews’ “within the veil”.

senses.definition: Further in, the inner of an outer and an inner: of the most holy house, the inner court where the priests serve, the king’s inner court.

evidence.note: The cherubim were set “within the inner house”.
He built the inner court with three rows of hewn stone.
The inner doors of the house, “for the most holy place”.
The priests entering the gates of the inner court shall wear linen.
Whoever comes to the king into the inner court uncalled shall die, unless he hold out the golden sceptre; Est 5:1.
The pattern of the inner rooms and of the house of the covering.
The hope that enters “into the inner (τὸ ἐσώτερον) of the veil”.
The inner prison.

words.summary: To or at the inside: within the holy place, the house, the palace. Its tie to the root is that of פְּנִימִי, resting on form alone: no verse or cognate shows how “inward” comes from “face” or “turn”.

senses.definition: Into or on the inside of a house or holy place.

evidence.note: “Its blood was not brought into the holy place within.”
The cedar of the house within.
The gatekeepers told it to the king’s house within.
The priests went into the inner part of the house of Yahweh to cleanse it.
“The king’s daughter is all glorious within.”

words.summary: Once, of the front part of Solomon’s house, the nave in front of the inner shrine. Built on לִפְנֵי “before”; one use only.

senses.definition: The part of the house that lay in front of the inner shrine.

evidence.note: “The house, that is the temple in front (לִפְנָי), was forty cubits.”

words.summary: The corner of an altar, a house, a street or a wall, where the line turns; the stone laid at it; and of a people, its chiefs, on whom it stands. The text files it under a root פנן, but its use fits “turn”: the corner is where a wall turns, and later Hebrew uses פִּינָּה both for “a turn” and for “corner”. No cognate is certain; Ugaritic pnt “vertebrae” is possible.

senses.definition: The corner of an altar, a house, a roof, a stand, a wall or a street.

evidence.note: The horns of the altar on its four corners.
A wind struck the four corners of the house.
Better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than with a brawling woman.
She lies in wait at every corner.
Ahaz made altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
The Corner Gate; so Jer 31:38.
A day of the shofar against the high corner towers.

senses.definition: The stone laid at the corner, on which the building’s lines are set: the foundation of the earth, the stone Yahweh lays in Zion, and the stone the builders rejected.

evidence.note: “Who laid its cornerstone?” of the earth.
No stone shall be taken from Babylon for a corner or for foundations.
“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner, a sure foundation; he who believes shall not make haste.”
“The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.”
Jesus applies Psa 118:22 to himself, κεφαλὴν γωνίας; Peter to the rulers in Act 4:11.
Isa 28:16 and Psa 118:22 together (1Pe 2:6–7).
Built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ being the chief cornerstone (ἀκρογωνιαῖος).

senses.definition: In the plural, the chief men of a people, its cornerstones; once of the coming ruler from Judah.

evidence.note: “The corners of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel” presented themselves in the assembly.
“Draw near, all you corners of the people.”
The princes of Zoan have led Egypt astray, “the corner of its tribes”.
“From him the corner, from him the nail, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.”

evidence.locator: פִּנָּה → γωνία ×11, with γωνιῶν ×4 and γωνίαν ×2 (MACULA alignment); Psa.118.22 κεφαλὴν γωνίας

words.gloss: return; answer; (ethpeel) turn, turn back, be converted; (aphel) turn back, restore
words.summary: The Peshitta’s verb of this root. It keeps the Hebrew’s turning, and adds the sense “turn back, return” and, from returning a word, “answer”. It is the Peshitta’s word for the New Testament’s ἐπιστρέφω, so that the gospel’s “turn to God from idols” is said with the root of Hebrew “turn to me and be saved” (Isa 45:22) and “do not turn to idols” (Lev 19:4).

senses.definition: Come back to where one or a thing was.

evidence.note: “If it is not worthy, your peace will return to you.”
Men waiting for their lord, when he returns from the wedding.

senses.definition: Return a word: reply.

evidence.note: He did not answer her a word.
“Do you give no reply?”
Accused by the chief priests and elders, he gave no reply.

stems.gloss: turn, turn round; turn back, return; turn (to God)

senses.definition: Turn oneself round to look or speak.

evidence.note: Jesus turned and looked at Cephas.
Jesus turned and saw them following.

senses.definition: Go back to where one came from.

evidence.note: The shepherds returned, glorifying God.
If he turns back to you seven times in a day, saying, I repent.

senses.definition: Turn from idols, sins or error to God: the turning of repentance.

evidence.note: “How you turned to God from the worship of idols, to serve the living and true God.”
“Repent and turn, that your sins may be blotted out.”
That the Gentiles should repent and turn to God.
Turn from these vain things to the living God who made heaven and earth.
“You were straying like sheep, and now have returned to the shepherd of your souls”, after Isa 53:6.
When one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away (after Exo 34:34).
Isa 6:10 quoted: lest they understand with their heart, and turn, and I heal them.
“And you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

senses.definition: Turn something toward someone.

evidence.note: “Whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.”

senses.definition: Bring someone back to God from error; restore what was lost.

evidence.note: John “will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God”, and turn the hearts of the fathers to the children (Luk 1:17, after Mal 3:24).
If anyone wanders from the truth and one turns him back; he who turns a sinner from his error saves his soul from death (Jas 5:20).
“Will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s noun from פְּנָא: a turning back, of the Gentiles turning to God.

senses.definition: The turning of people to God, or their coming back.

evidence.note: Through Phoenicia and Samaria “telling of the conversion of the Gentiles”.
If their casting away is the reconciling of the world, what is their return but life from the dead?

cognates.gloss: front, face; presence; (ana pān, ina pān) before, in the presence of
cognates.note: Oracc’s glossaries give pānu “front” some 28,000 times, with the meanings “face, front, surface, appearance, presence, before, in front of, in the presence of, from before, because of”, and pānu “face” separately: the range of פָּנִים and of its prepositions לִפְנֵי and מִפְּנֵי, plural like the Hebrew.

evidence.locator: atae x000006850, pānātu [front] N (meanings: before, in front of, in the presence of)

cognates.note: The Akkadian adverb pāna “formerly” and adjective pānû “former, previous, ancient” show the same reckoning as Hebrew לְפָנִים “formerly”: what is in front is what has gone before.

A Neo-Assyrian verb glossed “face” and meaning “go in front, proceed”, made from pānu. It answers to the participle פֹּנֶה “facing, turned toward”, but is late and rare (30 uses), so recorded as possible.

Segert’s glossary gives pn, plural pnm, “face” and lpn “before”, comparing Hebrew pānîm, lipnê, Phoenician lpn and Akkadian pānū; his texts include idk lttn pnm “then she set (her) face”, the Hebrew נָתַן פָּנִים. Fisher sets beside it lpnm “forwards”.

evidence.note: “pn ‘face’, lpnm ‘forwards’, lpn ‘before’” (OCR read).

cognates.note: Segert glosses pnt (pl.?) “vertebrae”, with a query “cf. H. pinnā ‘corner’?”. If right, it is a joint or turning point of the body, as פִּנָּה is of a wall; both the meaning and the comparison are uncertain.

Krahmalkov: pnm “face”, in ḥz pnm “see the face of”, so possess (KAI 24), and “front, face” of a stele “his face to the west and his back to the east” (KAI 78), the face set against the back as in Exo 33:23.

cognates.gloss: before, in the presence of; before (in time)
cognates.note: Krahmalkov gives lpn “before, in the presence of” (KAI 24, “in the presence of earlier kings”), “before” in time (KAI 11, the queens “who were before me”), and lpny “predecessor; former”: the senses of לִפְנֵי.
Phoenician lpnm “earlier, before, in the past” (KAI 26: places that “were dangerous before”), the same form and sense as Hebrew לְפָנִים “formerly”.

cognates.gloss: road, entrance passage; canal; (adverbially, b-fnwt) in the direction of, in front of
cognates.note: Sabaean fnwt is a way in or a channel, and as an adverb “in the direction of, in front of”. Biella compares Ge’ez fenot “road, direction” and fena “in the direction of”, and Hebrew פָּנָה for the root sense “face”. It answers to לִפְנֵי “in front of” and the verb’s turning toward a direction.

cognates.gloss: send away (make go toward a place); way, road, direction
cognates.note: Fisher sets beside Ugaritic pn the Ge’ez verb fannawa “send away (i.e. make s.o. turn toward a direction)”, the noun fǝnot “way, road, journey” and fǝnna “toward, side”; Biella cites fenot “road, direction”. The link from “face” to “direction” is the verb’s own (פֹּנֶה “facing” a quarter), but the Ge’ez verb means “send”, so it is recorded as possible. Not yet checked in Dillmann or Leslau.

evidence.note: OCR read.

cognates.gloss: turn to or from; go; (לְמִפְנֵי רַמְשָׁא) toward evening
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic has the verb “turn to or from, go” (Targum Jonathan Gen 24:49; Onkelos Deu 29:17), and Onkelos renders Gen 24:63 לִפְנוֹת עֶרֶב by לְמִפְנֵי רַמְשָׁא “at the turning of evening”: the Hebrew idiom in its own Aramaic. Aramaic says “face” with another root (אַנְפִּין).

evidence.note: Targ. Y. Gen. 24:49; Targ. O. Deut. 29:17; Targ. O. Gen. 24:63 למִפְנֵי רמשא “towards evening”.

cognates.gloss: yard, open court in front of a house
cognates.note: Lane: “a yard, or an exterior court, i.e. a wide space, in front, or extending from the sides, of a house”. The space before a house would answer to פָּנִים “front”, but Arabic has no פנה “face” or “turn” beside it, and the root فني otherwise means “pass away, perish”, so the link is possible only.

doctrine.statement: Israel’s feasts are kept לִפְנֵי יְהוָה, “before Yahweh”: the sheaf and the loaves of firstfruits are waved before him, the Day of the coverings makes covering before him, and Israel rejoices before him seven days at the feast of booths (Lev 23:11, 20, 28, 40); three times a year every male appears before his face, not empty (Exo 23:17; Deu 16:16). The trumpets blown over the offerings are a memorial before God, and in war the alarm brings Israel to remembrance before Yahweh, and they are saved (Num 10:9–10). The ark goes before them to seek a resting place, and when it sets out his enemies flee from before him (Num 10:33–35; Psa 68:2). Hebrews says Christ entered not a holy place made with hands but heaven itself, “now to appear in the presence (πρόσωπον) of God for us” (Heb 9:24). From the verses: Israel’s worship was done in the presence Yahweh had placed among them, and that presence went before them and scattered their enemies; Christ now stands before God’s face on behalf of his people.

Yahweh tells Moses, “You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live”, and shows him his back only (Exo 33:20, 23); yet in the same chapter he speaks with Moses “face to face, as a man speaks to his friend” (Exo 33:11; Deu 34:10). Jacob says at Peniel, “I have seen God face to face”, and Hosea says he strove with God, “he strove with the angel and prevailed” (Gen 32:31; Hos 12:4–5); Gideon fears because he has seen the angel of Yahweh face to face (Jdg 6:22). Yahweh sends his angel before Israel with “my name is in him”, and Isaiah calls him “the angel of his face” who saved them (Exo 23:20–21; Isa 63:9). Paul says God has given “the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2Co 4:6). The psalmist hopes to behold God’s face in righteousness when he awakes (Psa 17:15), Jesus says the pure in heart shall see God (Mat 5:8), and Revelation says his servants “shall see his face” (Rev 22:4; 1Co 13:12). From the verses: no mortal man sees God’s own face; he was seen face to face in the angel who bore his name, his glory is now seen in the face of his Son, and the faithful are promised to see his face when they awake from death.

The priests bless Israel with Yahweh’s face: “Yahweh make his face shine on you and be gracious to you; Yahweh lift up his face on you and give you peace” (Num 6:25–26), and the psalmist prays, “cause your face to shine, and we shall be saved” (Psa 80:4, 8, 20). When Israel turns to other gods Yahweh hides his face (Deu 31:17–18); “your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you” (Isa 59:2); but he promises, “I will not hide my face from them any more, for I have poured out my spirit on the house of Israel” (Ezk 39:29). Peter calls Israel to repent and turn, “that times of refreshing may come from the face of the Lord” (Act 3:19). From the verses: Yahweh’s face turned toward a people is their blessing and salvation, sin turns it away, and its return is promised with the gift of his spirit and offered to those who turn back to him.

Yahweh “does not lift up faces nor take a bribe” (Deu 10:17), and Israel’s judges are not to lift up the face of the poor nor honour the face of the mighty, nor recognise faces in judgment, “for the judgment is God’s” (Lev 19:15; Deu 1:17; 16:19); the priests are rebuked for lifting up faces in the law (Mal 2:9). The New Testament puts the idiom into Greek: God is no προσωπολήμπτης, but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is accepted by him (Act 10:34–35); there is no προσωποληψία with God (Rom 2:11); God does not receive the face of man (Gal 2:6); believers are not to hold the faith of Christ with respect of persons (Jas 2:1, 9); the Father judges without respect of persons according to each one’s work (1Pe 1:17). From the verses: God judges by what a man does, not by his standing, and on that ground the Gentiles are accepted with Israel; his people must judge and receive one another the same way.

The law forbids Israel to turn to idols or to mediums (Lev 19:4, 31), and Yahweh hides his face when they turn to other gods (Deu 31:18). Through Isaiah he calls, “Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other”, and swears that every knee shall bow to him (Isa 45:22–23), which Paul applies to God’s judgment and to the name of Jesus (Rom 14:11; Php 2:10–11). Isaiah confesses, “we have turned each one to his own way, and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all” (Isa 53:6), and Peter, quoting the chapter, writes, “you were as sheep going astray, but are now returned to the shepherd and overseer of your souls” (1Pe 2:24–25). The Thessalonians “turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God” (1Th 1:9), where the Peshitta uses this root. From the verses: salvation is offered to every nation on the one condition of turning to the one God, the turning away of each to his own way was laid on his servant, and the gospel’s call to turn from idols is Isaiah’s call carried to the Gentiles.

Isaiah’s voice cries, “In the wilderness clear the way of Yahweh” (Isa 40:3), and through Malachi Yahweh says, “I send my messenger, and he will clear the way before me; and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple”, the messenger being Elijah sent before the day of Yahweh (Mal 3:1, 23–24). All four gospels apply Isa 40:3 to John the Baptist (Mat 3:3; Mrk 1:3; Luk 3:4; Jhn 1:23), and Jesus applies Mal 3:1 to him, reading “before your face… before you”, and says John is the Elijah who was to come (Mat 11:10, 14; 17:12). Zacharias says John will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, turning the hearts of the fathers to the children (Luk 1:17, 76). From the verses: the way cleared for Yahweh’s coming was cleared by John for Jesus, so that Yahweh came to his people in his Son, whom he sent and in whom he was at work.

Yahweh says, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner (פִּנָּה), a sure foundation; he who believes shall not make haste” (Isa 28:16), and the psalm says, “the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this is Yahweh’s doing” (Psa 118:22–23). Jesus applies the psalm to himself against the chief priests and elders (Mat 21:42), and Peter tells the rulers that Jesus is the stone “rejected by you builders” (Act 4:11). Peter and Paul join Isa 28:16 to it: those who believe are built on him as living stones, and to those who disbelieve he is a stone of stumbling (1Pe 2:4–8; Rom 9:33); the household of God is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ being the chief cornerstone (Eph 2:20). From the verses: the builders were Israel’s rulers who rejected Jesus; God laid him as the corner on which his house is set, and men stand or fall by their faith in him.

note: Draft from the brief and the text, 2026-11-13. (1) The DB keys the root פנה; פִּנָּה “corner” is keyed under פננ (q.bv.ab) and is included here with its own root, on the use (a corner is where a wall turns) and later Hebrew פִּינָּה “turn, movement; corner” (Jastrow s.v. פִּינָּה, Q00720, Rabbinic, not a cognate). The other פננ words, פְּנִינִים “corals” (q.bv.ac) and the name Peninnah (q.bv.ad), are left out: nothing ties them to “turn” or “face”; a reviewer may want a פננ entry for them. (2) q.bu.aa’s three tokens with no stem (Psa 118:22; Pro 7:12; 2Ch 28:24) are the noun פִּנָּה counted under the verb too; Zep 3:15 is the piel. (3) לִפְנֵי and מִפְּנֵי have no bdb key of their own: their tokens are filed under פָּנִים (q.bu.ab). (4) Names left for name entries: Jephunneh (q.bu.ag, j.co.ad) and Penuel (q.bu.af, q.bu.ai; a person in 1Ch 4:4 and 8:25, and a place, Gen 32:31). (5) Fisher’s and Segert’s readings are from OCR; check the page images. Ge’ez not yet checked in Dillmann or Leslau; Syriac פְּנָא stems are from SEDRA’s form codes on the BFBS text (peal Mat 10:13; pael Mat 15:23; ethpeel passim; aphel Luk 1:16) and want checking in Payne Smith. (6) Biblical Aramaic and Syriac say “face” with אַנְפִּין / ܐܦܐ of another root, so no Aramaic noun stands beside פָּנִים. (7) The prepare-the-way doctrine reads Mal 3:1 as Yahweh coming in his Son, consistent with God manifestation; flagged for the user’s review.
